column3: The Hebrew repeats Solomon’s name with his desire; BSB uses “he.”
The Hebrew explicitly names Solomon as the recipient of the appearance; BSB uses “him.”
The Hebrew says setting His Name there as the purpose of consecrating; BSB joins them with “by.”
The Hebrew retains an explicit “you” at the beginning.
The Hebrew says a man will not be cut off from the throne; BSB renders this as never failing to have a man on it.
The Hebrew joins you and your sons with “and”; BSB uses “or.”
The Hebrew retains the face of the ground and God’s face, and calls Israel a proverb and a taunt; BSB uses land, presence, and an object of scorn and ridicule.
The Hebrew says this house will be high, without explicitly naming rubble; BSB says the temple becomes a heap of rubble.
The Hebrew leaves the speakers unnamed and uses an ordinary saying verb; BSB supplies “others” who answer.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats Hiram’s name and narrates his supplies before Solomon’s gift; BSB rearranges this.
The Hebrew retains the image of things not being right in his eyes; BSB says he was not pleased.
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed; BSB identifies Hiram.
The Hebrew narrates Hiram sending, without explicitly marking it as earlier than the surrounding actions.
The Hebrew names Millo; BSB renders it “the supporting terraces.”
The Hebrew says Pharaoh went up and uses collective singular “the Canaanite”; BSB has attacked and plural Canaanites.
The Hebrew uses the ordinary building verb without separately marking rebuilding.
The Hebrew says “in the land,” without explicitly naming Judah.
The Hebrew lists store cities, chariot cities, and horsemen’s cities separately; BSB combines the storage and military purposes.
The Hebrew calls them sons of Israel; BSB has Israelites.
The Hebrew calls the remaining descendants their sons and explicitly says they remained after them.
The Hebrew calls his military men simply men of war, without the first possessive “his.”
The Hebrew begins “These”; BSB says “They were also.”
The Hebrew leaves the builder unnamed and names Millo; BSB supplies Solomon and “the supporting terraces.”
The Hebrew calls the completed building the house; BSB uses temple.
The Hebrew retains the sea’s lip and the name Edom; BSB uses shore and rearranges the place references.
The Hebrew calls the sailors men of ships who know the sea, without a separate serving verb.
The Hebrew uses ordinary coming, taking, and bringing verbs and explicitly names King Solomon; BSB uses sailing, importing, and delivering and names only Solomon.
